display.title: The Alter Rebbe Frees the Chassan, Part 2
display.summary_short: On Chof-Beis Shevat, a story of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka's care for a shy young guest; then the Alter Rebbe raises the ransom by thanking a stingy rich man for his rusty coin.
display.summary_long: On the yahrzeit of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, Chof-Beis Shevat, the storyteller shares a story he heard from a man who visited her as a shy little boy: she served him a big portion of ice cream herself, so he would not go without. The lesson is to offer guests food and drink without waiting for them to ask. Then the story of the captured chassan continues. With one sharp look the Alter Rebbe silences the angry police chief, who agrees to free the chassan for a thousand rubles by nightfall. The Rav's list of donors comes to less than a hundred, but the Alter Rebbe insists on going first to the stingy rich man. When he hands over his famous rusty coin, the Alter Rebbe thanks him warmly and blesses him. Again and again the rich man calls them back with more, until he breaks down and explains the vow he made years ago, and then gives the whole sum. The chassan is freed, the wedding is joyful, and the next morning brings a surprising gift. The lesson: see the good in every Jew and praise it.
display.lesson: Ahavas Yisroel means seeing what a person does do, not what he doesn't, and thanking him for it; then he will do more and more good. Offer guests what they need before they have to ask.
